title: Big-file sharing service lets a user crown themselves boss
product: IBM Aspera Faspex 5 (large-file transfer and sharing server)
eli5: A tool companies use to send huge files can be fooled by one specially written message into giving someone full control.
analogy: A hotel guest who words a room-service request in one exact way and is handed the master key and the manager's office.
impact: Someone could read, swap or delete every file shared through it, and change who is allowed in.
who: Organisations running their own Aspera Faspex server. Ordinary people who just receive files from it needn't do anything.
todo: IT teams should update Faspex to version 5.0.19 PL1 now.
tech_type: Authorisation bypass leading to full administrative privileges (CWE-863, incorrect authorization)
tech_how: IBM says a crafted message sent to Faspex 5 can bypass user authorisation checks and grant full administrative rights. The bulletin text describes the attacker as an 'authorized user', yet IBM's CVSS vector is network-based with no privileges required (PR:N), so treat internet-facing instances as reachable without a login until IBM clarifies. With admin rights an attacker controls all packages, users, shared inboxes and settings, which makes it attractive for data theft; older Faspex 4 flaws were exploited by ransomware gangs in 2023. No public proof of concept, exploitation or IOCs have been reported so far, and IBM lists no workaround. Restrict Faspex web access to trusted networks until patched and review admin accounts and recent configuration changes.
tech_versions: Affects IBM Aspera Faspex 5.0.0 to 5.0.19. Fixed in 5.0.19 PL1 (Linux); check the faspex-core container image reports '5.0.19 (1ce4b13, Fix Pack: 1)'. IBM bulletin published 7 Nov 2026. Not in CISA KEV.

title: SonicWall office VPNs let people skip the extra security check
product: SonicWall SonicOS SSL-VPN (Gen 7 and Gen 8 firewalls using SAML sign-in)
cvss_note: SonicWall's rating (some trackers list 7.5 under CVSS 3.1)
eli5: Some company firewalls that let staff work from home can be tricked into skipping the second login step, and attackers are already doing it.
analogy: A gym with a turnstile that scans your face, but a side gate where the old paper membership card still works on its own.
impact: Someone holding a stolen password could get into the company network without the code from your phone.
who: Companies using SonicWall firewalls for staff remote access. Home users and staff themselves needn't do anything.
todo: IT teams should install SonicWall's latest firewall update straight away and check recent remote logins.
tech_type: Authentication enforcement weakness allowing SAML and MFA bypass (CWE-308, use of single-factor authentication)
tech_how: On SonicOS SSL-VPN configured for SAML authentication, a user holding valid credentials for an alternate (non-SAML) authentication method can authenticate without passing the SAML flow, sidestepping any MFA enforced through the identity provider. The attacker needs working credentials (for example from phishing, password reuse or earlier breaches); there is no evidence of unauthenticated access or code execution. SonicWall PSIRT (advisory SNWLID-2026-0014) says it investigated a report of potential exploitation, and CISA has listed it as exploited. Attackers and scale are not public, ransomware use is listed as unknown, and no IOCs have been published. No workaround is offered: review SSL-VPN logs for sessions that skipped SAML, reset credentials for affected users and restrict which authentication methods the VPN accepts.
tech_versions: Affects Gen 7 SonicOS 7.3.3-7015 and earlier and Gen 8 SonicOS 8.2.2-8015 and earlier (physical and virtual). Fixed in 7.3.4-7013 and later (7.3.4-7015 released 5 Nov 2026) and 8.2.3-8015. Gen 6 and older are end of support with no fix. Added to CISA KEV on 6 Nov 2026 (federal due date reported as 20 Nov 2026).

title: Very long password opens locked doors on Alpine servers
product: OpenSSH on Alpine Linux and other musl-based systems without PAM
eli5: On some small Linux servers, typing a ridiculously long password lets you log in to accounts that were never meant to have one.
analogy: A cloakroom attendant who, when your ticket is too long to read, just shrugs and hands over a coat that was never checked in.
impact: A stranger on the internet could log straight in to a server and take it over, and attackers started trying within hours.
who: People running Alpine Linux servers that accept passwords over SSH. Ordinary computer and phone users needn't do anything.
todo: Update OpenSSH and restart it, or switch off password logins and use keys only.
tech_type: Authentication bypass via crypt() edge case in non-PAM sshd password checking
tech_how: Alpine's openssh-server is built without PAM, so sshd verifies passwords itself with crypt(). Accounts with no password have '*' in the shadow field; that is too short to hold a salt, so sshd borrows the salt of another account's real hash (behaviour added in 2016 for CVE-2016-6210). For $5$/$6$ hashes, musl's crypt() rejects passwords over 256 bytes by returning '*', which then matches the stored '*', so the login is accepted. Preconditions: non-PAM sshd (or UsePAM no), PasswordAuthentication yes (the default), an account whose password field is '*', and at least one other local account with a $5$ or $6$ hash. The attacker needs network access, a passwordless account name (e.g. alpine or root) and a password of 257 to 1,024 bytes; it works on every attempt. glibc-based Linux, PAM-based setups, non-Linux systems and Dropbear are not affected. Now exploited: Previdian saw the first attempt under nine hours after the CVE was published and confirmed root on an Alpine honeypot (eight attempts from 89.116.89[.]18, running id, uname and hostname). Not yet in CISA KEV. Hunt for 'Accepted password for' on passwordless accounts in /var/log/messages.
tech_versions: Fixed in OpenSSH 10.6p2 (5 Nov 2026), which refuses a match when the stored field is under four characters. Alpine fixed packages ship in 3.21.10, 3.22.8, 3.23.8 and 3.24.4, with fixes back to the 3.16 branch. Tiny-cloud images 3.18.11 to 3.24.3 become exposed once any $6$ hash exists. Workaround: PasswordAuthentication no, check with sshd -t, then restart sshd. Other musl systems (Buildroot, Yocto, OpenWrt with OpenSSH) should be checked.

title: AI server software handing admin keys to strangers
eli5: A tool companies use to run AI models treats strangers as the boss if they claim to be calling from inside the building, and attackers are already doing it.
analogy: A switchboard that gives full access to any caller who says 'I'm ringing from upstairs', without checking which line they're really on.
impact: Attackers can take over the AI servers, steal cloud keys and run their own programs on the company's machines.
who: Companies and teams running GPUStack. Everyday users needn't do anything.
todo: Update GPUStack to version 2.2.2 or later straight away.
tech_type: Authentication bypass by origin/IP spoofing (CWE-287, CWE-290, CWE-346); plus SAML signature verification bypass (CWE-347)
tech_how: CVE-2026-102895: with force_auth_localhost defaulting to false, GPUStack grants admin to any request from a loopback address. Behind a same-host reverse proxy every external request appears to come from 127.0.0.1, and attackers can also send a spoofed X-GPUStack-Real-IP: 127.0.0.1 header. Remote and unauthenticated. The vendor confirms exploitation in the wild against a v2.1.1 deployment: attackers gained admin, stole cloud keys, minted admin tokens and pushed rogue YAML configs/custom backends to run reverse shells on worker nodes. CVE-2026-102894 (CVSS 9.1, not exploited): /auth/saml/callback issues a login token from a Base64 XML username without checking signature, issuer or validity window, and is enabled even when SAML isn't configured; replay is possible. No IOCs published.
tech_versions: CVE-2026-102895 affects all versions before 2.2.0 (fixed in 2.2.0); CVE-2026-102894 affects 0.7.1 up to before 2.2.2 (fixed in 2.2.2). Interim mitigations: set force_auth_localhost=true, strip X-GPUStack-Real-IP at the proxy, block external access to /auth/saml/callback. Not in CISA KEV as of this update. Advisories GHSA-gj9m-f8ph-pmhr and GHSA-62m9-f875-rqw6.

title: Shop software lets strangers run code from the login page
product: Apache OFBiz (open-source business and e-commerce suite)
eli5: Free software that runs online shops and company accounts has several holes that let outsiders take control without logging in.
analogy: A sign-in book at a factory gate where writing certain words in the 'name' box starts the machines inside.
impact: Attackers could take over the business system and get at orders, customer details and finances.
who: Businesses running Apache OFBiz. Shoppers and ordinary users needn't do anything.
todo: Upgrade Apache OFBiz to version 24.09.08 now.
tech_type: Unauthenticated code injection / remote code execution (CWE-94), auth bypass (CWE-288), hard-coded JWT key (CWE-321)
tech_how: A large batch of fixes. Key pre-auth issues: CVE-2026-83542 (CVSS 9.8), RCE via widget injection on the login page; CVE-2026-68524, RCE via attacker-controlled screen definition loading; CVE-2026-73578, saved-view authorisation bypass with RCE impact; CVE-2026-105330, a hard-coded cryptographic key in JWT authentication giving unauthenticated admin access. Authenticated issues include unsandboxed Groovy compilation from a service parameter (CVE-2026-82912, 8.8), Groovy sandbox escapes in widget expressions (CVE-2026-82960, 8.8) and code execution by VIEW-only Content Manager users (CVE-2026-84183, 8.8), plus path traversal, SQL injection, XXE and SSRF. OFBiz has a history of rapid exploitation, though no attacks or public PoC are reported yet.
tech_versions: All Apache OFBiz versions before 24.09.08 are affected; fixed in 24.09.08. Several CVEs are still awaiting scores. Not in CISA KEV.

title: Code storage tool lets banned users sneak back in
eli5: A popular tool where companies keep their software parts lets locked-out staff log in again, and lets some users pretend to be the admin.
analogy: A gym that cancels your membership but still lets you in if you wave your old card from the partner gym down the road.
impact: Someone who shouldn't have access could tamper with the software a company builds and ships to customers.
who: Companies running Nexus Repository 3. Ordinary users needn't do anything.
todo: Update Nexus Repository to 3.98.0, then review logins and rotate signing keys.
tech_type: Improper authentication of locked SSO accounts (CWE-1390); missing authorisation enabling header-based login (CWE-862)
tech_how: CVE-2026-113373 (CVSS 4.0 9.1): on SAML or OAuth2 sign-in the server doesn't check whether the local account is disabled or locked, so a locked user with valid identity-provider credentials gets a fresh session with their old roles. CVE-2026-113374 (8.6): a user holding only nexus:capabilities:create can enable Rut Auth header logins without realm admin rights, after which a remote attacker can log in as any user, including admin, with no password. Others: SQL injection in the Reindex Search by Pattern task (7.7, off by default), signing passphrase/key exposure to read-admin accounts (7.1 each), stored XSS in the OCI Attestations tab (6.3) and a group-repository authorisation bypass (5.3). All require an authenticated account. No exploitation or public exploit reported.
tech_versions: CVE-2026-113373 affects Pro 3.86.0 to 3.97.x; CVE-2026-113374 affects all CE and Pro 3.0.0 before 3.98.0. Fixed in 3.98.0, which also disables stored script execution unless nexus.scripts.allowExecution=true. Updating doesn't undo abuse: rotate signing keys, review login logs and remove rogue Rut Auth capabilities and realms. Not in CISA KEV.

title: Cluster rule-keeper lets one team grab the whole system
eli5: A tool that enforces rules on big shared computer systems can be fooled into giving one small team power over everyone else's work.
analogy: A block of flats where any tenant can leave a note for the caretaker, and the caretaker happily unlocks other people's flats because the note asked nicely.
impact: Someone with limited access to one corner of a company's systems could take over the lot and tamper with other teams' apps.
who: Companies running Kubernetes with Kyverno installed. Everyday users needn't do anything.
todo: Upgrade Kyverno to version 1.19.2 or later and check who is allowed to write policies.
tech_type: Cross-namespace privilege escalation and path traversal in namespaced policy handling (confused deputy)
tech_how: Kyverno's controllers run with broad cluster permissions, and several namespaced policy types were not confined to their own namespace. A principal who can create namespaced Policies (typically a namespace admin, so PR:L) can: make a generate rule target another namespace or a cluster-scoped kind (CVE-2026-122302); overwrite resources elsewhere via NamespacedMutatingPolicy (CVE-2026-122303) or its targetMatchConstraints.expression (CVE-2026-122313); escape the namespace through the cleanup controller (CVE-2026-122304); or use '../' segments in context.apiCall URLs (CVE-2026-122310) and the namespaced CEL engine (CVE-2026-122311) to call arbitrary API paths. The result is actions performed with Kyverno's own service-account rights, up to creating cluster-wide MutatingWebhookConfigurations. Public advisories include reproductions; no in-the-wild exploitation reported. Audit RBAC for who can create Kyverno namespaced policies and review recent cluster-scoped changes made by the Kyverno service accounts.
tech_versions: Published 5 Nov 2026 in a batch of around 49 Kyverno advisories (the rest rated 7.2 to 8.7, mostly DoS and smaller escalations). Affected ranges vary: 1.16.0 or 1.17.0 through 1.19.1. Fixed in 1.19.2 for most; check each GitHub advisory, as some list no fixed version yet and CVE-2026-122313's record names 1.19.2 as affected. Not in CISA KEV.

title: An old iPhone bug is back in spies' toolkits
product: Apple iOS, iPadOS, macOS, Safari, tvOS and watchOS
eli5: A two-year-old Apple bug, fixed long ago, is being used again against people whose devices never got updated.
analogy: A forged wax seal on a letter: once the seal looks right, the post room stops checking who really sent it.
impact: Visiting a hacked website on an old iPhone or Mac could let attackers steal your logins and browser cookies.
who: Anyone with an Apple device stuck on old software. Up to date since mid-2024? You're fine.
todo: Open Settings, then General, then Software Update, and install the latest version.
tech_type: Improper authentication leading to Pointer Authentication (PAC) bypass in WebKit/Safari
tech_how: An attacker who already has arbitrary memory read/write (typically via a separate WebKit remote code execution bug) can use CVE-2024-27834 to bypass Pointer Authentication, turning a renderer bug into reliable code execution. First shown as a zero-day at Pwn2Own Vancouver in March 2024. Sekoia reports a zero-click, drive-by chain pairing a WebKit RCE flaw with this PAC bypass, delivered via compromised legitimate sites, look-alike sites and a supply-chain compromise of the Plerdy SEO Tracker analytics script; malicious JavaScript profiles visitors, then drops an info-stealer that grabs browser cookies. Attributed with moderate to high confidence to APT29 (Cozy Bear / Midnight Blizzard). No IOCs published in the coverage reviewed.
tech_versions: Fixed May 2024 in iOS and iPadOS 16.7.8 and 17.5, macOS Sonoma 14.5, tvOS 17.5, watchOS 10.5 and Safari 17.5; anything older is exposed. Added to CISA KEV on 4 Nov 2026 (federal due date 18 Nov 2026).

title: A booby-trapped picture upload can rewrite a Rails website
product: Ruby on Rails (Active Storage with ImageMagick)
cvss_note: Rails' own rating; NVD score not yet published
eli5: Websites built with Rails that resize uploaded pictures can be tricked by a special image into saving files anywhere on the server.
analogy: A photo shop told to frame a picture finds hidden instructions on the back saying 'also file this in the manager's drawer', and does it.
impact: A stranger could plant files on the website's server and possibly take it over, without needing an account.
who: Teams running Rails apps that let people upload images. Just using such websites? Nothing to do.
